newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan urges non-interference in Afghanistan.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan urges non-interference in Afghanistan.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev, speaking ahead of a special summit of CIS leaders, urged other countries on Friday not to interfere in the internal affairs of war-torn Afghanistan.

"Unfortunately, the interests of many great states are focused there (Afghanistan)," Nazarbayev told reporters. "Now what is important is not to meddle in the internal affairs." CIS leaders were to meet in the Kazakh capital Almaty later on Friday to discuss Afghanistan.
The summit was called by Russia to mull the possible impact on the region of the fall of the Afghan capital to the radical Islamic Taleban militia.

Nazarbayev said Kazakhstan, which has no borders with Afghanistan and no political problems with it, could come out with a peace initiative, but he gave no details. He said he had discussed this issue with Iran, Turkey and Pakistan.
"I think Kazakhstan is well-positioned to do this as Russia and some other states are not correctly perceived here," said Nazarbayev.

Russian officials warned this week that the Taleban takeover of most of Afghanistan could destabilise the former Soviet republics in Central Asia. Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan all have borders with Afghanistan.
